provenance.citation: Kakas, A. C., Kowalski, R. A., & Toni, F. (1992). Abductive Logic Programming. Journal of Logic and Computation, 2(6), 719–770.
provenance.locus: Section 1.1 (introductory example): grass-is-wet — wet ← rained; wet ← sprinkler-on; observation wet; abducibles {rained, sprinkler-on}; the two minimal abductive explanations are {rained} and {sprinkler-on}. The same section introduces integrity constraints as the mechanism that rules out explanations.
provenance.notes: The grass-wet program is the paper's running introductory example of abduction in logic programming. Both singleton explanations are minimal and IC-consistent; enumeration order (size then lex) lists {rained} before {sprinkler-on} alphabetically: 'rained' < 'sprinkler-on'.

input.intent: explain the wet grass observation (KKT 1992 Section 1)

expected.notes: Two minimal explanations per KKT 1992; the empty set and the pair {rained,sprinkler_on} are excluded (non-explaining / non-minimal).
